title: Let one shipping policy quote for every request thread

blocks.text: The checkout page quotes shipping through one `ShippingPolicy` object that every request thread calls. The carrier's rate table is a remote service, and a lookup can take 300 ms. The version in production, `ByWeightV1`, gives the right price in every unit test, yet support has tickets from customers who were quoted the price of somebody else's parcel, and only at busy hours.

Write `quoteCents` in `ByWeight`, in `src/main/java/practice/ShippingQuotes.java`. It gives every parcel the price `ByWeightV1` gives it when called on its own: billable kilograms (the grams rounded up, at least 1) times the zone's rate, plus 20 % for the zone `island`. One `ByWeight` serves every thread at once, and a quote must not wait for another parcel's rate lookup. Leave `ByWeightV1` as it is. About three lines in total.

cases.says: a parcel is priced at its billable kilograms times its zone's rate, with 20 % more for island parcels
a quote that waits on its rate lookup while another quote runs to the end through the same policy still prices its own parcel
a quote for another zone finishes while one rate lookup is still waiting

origin.section: A Strategy Object Is Shared, So a Field in It Is Shared State

concepts: One strategy instance serves every thread, so fields that carry per-call values between its steps mix concurrent calls; keeping those values in locals or a value the call owns fixes it.
Making the shared fields volatile doesn't stop the race and made it far more frequent; synchronized makes it correct but makes every caller queue behind one lock, including behind a slow call.
